_comment: Shared source of truth for which live pages are essays. Read by scripts/audit-content-flow.mjs (Node) and scripts/check-density.sh (embedded Python), so the two content gates cannot drift on which pages count as an essay the way they did on 2026-08-22. See design/density-budget.md, 'Page-type scope,' for what qualifies a page for this list and what each field controls. Redirect stubs (e.g. toccata-expressiveness-upgrade*.html) do not belong here: they carry no prose and are not in site-manifest.json's live pages.

essays.reason: Hosted guest piece by Moose, explicitly outside the site's checked claim set; owner confirmed it stays untouched. 191 visible words, far under the normal ceiling.

Routing page carrying one claim, one action, and the collision-sim demo inline. Rebuilt 24 August 2026 to the Apple test: the status block, the live API panel and the keep-reading row were cut, leaving hero and demo. It now measures 122 visible words against the general 300 ceiling, so it needs no raised budget. The previous 340 budget existed for three demo cards that no longer exist.

_essays_removed_2026_08_29: argent-explained.html was listed here and on per_section_pages at once, with the same one-line reason on both: "Reference page carrying a live repository table and an embedded demo." That is a per-section reason, not an essay reason. This list exempts a page from the 60-word paragraph cap because continuous prose is the product and a deliberate run-on is voice; a reference page a reader consults for a repo table is not that, and the exemption was hiding one 90-word paragraph. Removed from essays, kept on per_section_pages, paragraph shortened. It never had extended_word_limit, so audit-content-flow.mjs is unaffected, and check-visible-words.mjs skips per_section_pages outright, so its whole-page budget is unchanged too.
_per_section_pages_comment: Which pages hold the 300-word ceiling from design/STANDARD.md's 'The 300-word surface' at the whole-page level (checked by scripts/check-visible-words.mjs, the default for every page not listed here or in essays above) versus at the per-section level (checked by scripts/check-visible-sections.mjs: no unbroken run of prose over 300 words between structural breaks). Decision recorded in HANDOFF.md, 'Decisions taken this session,' 2026-08-23: the whole-page cap fits a demo, the homepage, or a routing page, where the entire page is the surface. It does not fit a long-form guide or a reference page, where length is the content and structure (headings, tables, figures, details, lists, card/grid components) already breaks it into scannable pieces -- applying the literal cap there would hide most of the page, which is the inverted disclosure design/STANDARD.md itself bans. Every page below was judged on what it actually is (a taught guide or a lookup reference with real headings and card/table structure throughout), not carried over automatically from any other page-type list in this repo: design/density-budget.md's 'Answer and status pages' category answers a different question (how many words sit before the first interactive element) and does not determine this one. Demos, index.html, and routing pages are not listed here and keep the hard whole-page ceiling by default; three of the pages currently over that ceiling (demos/node-cost.html, demos/parameterless.html, demos/fair-launch.html) are deliberately not listed here even though they are over budget, because they are hard-ceiling pages owned by a different concurrent pass and belong on the whole-page rule once fixed, not on this list.

per_section_pages.reason: 3,287-word mining guide: two-market economics, ASIC/fee analysis, a mining walkthrough with OS-specific setup instructions. Headings, figures, an ordered learning-steps list, and multiple guide-detail/deep-dive disclosures already break it into sections a reader can skip between.

Builder guide: route selection, per-product requirements, verification checks, Toccata prep work. Structured throughout with heading sections, an api-command-grid, a builder-console grid, and a reference-grid; not a routing page of bare link cards, it teaches what to check and why.

The site's design-tradeoffs argument: what other networks already do well, where Kaspa spends its design budget, current boundaries and execution risk. Argued in sections under real headings, with a view-switch component and check-grid, not a single essay-length pour.

Narrative history piece (DAGLabs, the fair-launch decision, mainnet without a premine, the Golang-to-Rust rewrite). Long-form by nature; broken into dated sections with headings and a source list, not a single run.

Ground-up crypto explainer: what a blockchain is, six places it works, six places it doesn't, when a coin has a price. Teaching guide with a decision-grid, a timeline, and lane-grids sectioning it throughout.

The site's status tracker: a full status table, evidence sections, and a common-questions block. A reader consults one row or one question, not the whole page top to bottom; broken by tables, a quick-grid, and a reference-grid throughout.
The core explainer: parallel blocks, GHOSTDAG, fast-vs-final, what's live. Long by necessity for a first-explanation page; broken into headed sections with a transaction-rail and summary-grid.

Source index: what settles a claim, per-topic source lists, a full page map. Explicitly a lookup reference (the site's equivalent of a bibliography), sectioned with headings and multiple source-list grids.

KIP/KCC status tracker, already one of density-budget.md's named reference pages for the same reason: a reader arrives already knowing which proposal they want. Table-driven, headed sections throughout.

Risk table plus an embedded security-budget demo and two short prose sections. Its surface is seven table rows, the demo's own controls and readouts, and about 200 words of prose; the whole-page 300-word ceiling would have to hide the table or the demo to pass, which is the inverted disclosure design/STANDARD.md bans. Moved here from essays 2026-08-29; see _essays_removed_2026_08_29b.

_essays_removed_2026_08_29b: skeptical-case.html was listed under essays with the reason "Argues a case in continuous prose ... 1,555 visible words". That stopped being true before this pass: the page was already a seven-row risk table with per-cell disclosures, not continuous prose, and it measured 417 visible words. The essay exemption also waived the 60-word paragraph cap on a page whose longest paragraph was 155 words and sat inside a closed <details> inside a table cell. Rewritten 2026-08-29 as a risk table plus one interactive demo (#security-budget-demo) and two short prose sections: 721 visible words, none of them hidden, longest paragraph 54. Same shape as utxo-vs-accounts.html and argent-explained.html below, so it moves to per_section_pages, where the structural-break rule measures it and the paragraph cap applies.
_pages_merged_2026_09_02: start-here.html, utxo-vs-accounts.html and argent-explained.html were merged into index.html, what-is-kaspa.html#utxo and build-on-kaspa.html#argent and are redirect stubs now, so they carry no prose for either content gate to measure.
